**Findings (real text; old revisions, duplicates, popularity and outcomes are synthetic):**
- **Growth alone hurts:** hit@1 falls from 0.304 to 0.209 (world A) and from 0.278 to 0.188 (world B) between 25% and 100% of the stream. About 16% of retained rows are superseded versions, and 8% to 10% of top-1 results are stale.
- **Free byte savings (equivalent in both stages in both worlds):**
  - int8 keeps 32% of total bytes (−68%) with a retrieval difference of at most 0.0002.
  - Age-tiered storage keeps 44% to 53%.
  - Block-fp16 (−42%) gives bit-identical retrieval.
- **Supersession by structural key plus revision stamp:** −35% bytes, stale top-1 share to 0, hit@1 +0.014 to +0.017 and MRR about +0.030 in both worlds. It is Holm-significant in both stages in both worlds. A store with no old versions sees no gain and no harm (−0.0005 and +0.0011). The headline depends on a store carrying about 16% superseded rows and on revision stamps being available. Without stamps, latest arrival wins, and the gain drops by about a third.
- **Exact-duplicate suppression:** −11% rows, retrieval equivalent, MRR +0.005.
- **What fails:**
  - Cosine-based revision detection loses quality (keep-first merging −0.0044 at 0.95 and −0.041 at 0.70 hit@1; keep-newest loses about 0.009 on revision-free streams).
  - Anchor-summary rows save only 19.5% of bytes at −0.002 to −0.0075.
  - Every byte-cap eviction arm is neither equivalent nor non-inferior on uniform queries. Here value-based beats recency (the opposite of the earlier routing-memory result), and its effect needs informative feedback, since a random-credit control loses 0.05 to 0.09.
- **Closed-loop routing:** retrieval from an unbounded store captures only 4% to 12% of the oracle gain on the topic-dependent world. No end-to-end gain is claimed.

**Caveats:** absolute retrieval is low (hit@1 about 0.2 on near-sibling fragments), queries are clean with no typos, and latency was not measured. The ±0.01 equivalence margin can hide small losses. Several controls ran after the main stages on confirm seeds, and the worker flagged them as post-hoc.

**Recommendation (opt-in, proposals only):** structural-key supersession with revision stamps, age-tiered or int8 storage, and keep exact-duplicate suppression. Not recommended: cosine merging, eviction, and summary rows.
